claim: Because the trim scans only messages from start (this call's baseline), an earlier call's history is never cut.

Only messages from ``start`` (this call's baseline) are scanned, so an
    earlier call's history is never cut.

Falsifying input: the store's conversation shrank or was replaced between the baseline read and the trim read, so `start` no longer marks this call's first message; or a baseline count taken while another writer appended to the same conversation outside the turn lock.

claim: The trim docstring says the read, the scan and the truncate_messages call are each guarded and logged at ERROR, as is a store with no truncate_messages, so a cleanup failure never replaces the call's own result.
source_excerpt:
The read, the scan of the stored messages and the ``truncate_messages``
    call are each guarded and logged at ERROR, as is a store with no
    ``truncate_messages``, because the caller is about to return or raise the
    call's own result, which must not be replaced by a cleanup failure.

claim: A CancelledError raised while _trim_unanswered_tool_use is awaiting store.get_conversation (inside the inner try) reaches the outer `except asyncio.CancelledError` and runs the full rollback to the baseline.
verify_hint: Check the nesting of the inner `try`/`except Exception` (623-637) inside the outer `try` whose `except asyncio.CancelledError` is at line 638 in `query_database_impl_with_widgets`.
evidence: query_database.py: both _trim_unanswered_tool_use call sites (630-632 inside the inner `except Exception` handler, 635-637 after the inner try) sit inside the outer `try` opened at line 619, whose first handler is `except asyncio.CancelledError` at 638. In _trim_unanswered_tool_use (285-294) the get_conversation await is guarded only by `except Exception`, which does not catch CancelledError (a BaseException), so a cancel there propagates out of the helper to the caller's outer try. The 638 handler calls _rollback_conversation(agent, queued_id, baseline_user.id, baseline_messages) (646-648), a synchronous truncate to the baseline length, then re-raises (649). For a cancel raised at 630, the handler's own `raise` at 633 is never reached, and the CancelledError still propagates to the 638 handler. Absolute-input trace: a cancel while awaiting store.get_conversation at line 285 goes to 638 and rolls back to baseline_messages. The rejection line about truncate_messages returning None concerns a different subject and is not relied on.

claim: _UnscannableReadStore assumes the trim's get_conversation is the third read once armed and that appending a bare object() makes `_first_unanswered_tool_use` raise (no `.role`), while the unarmed history read still returns the real conversation.
verify_hint: Check `_first_unanswered_tool_use` in `src/sqllens/tools/query_database.py` (reads `message.role` from messages[start:]) and the `get_conversation` calls in `send_message` in `src/sqllens/agent/core/agent/agent.py`.
evidence: Test class at tests/unit/test_query_database_tool_history.py:325-337 (the cited 592-604 does not exist; file is 397 lines). Read order once armed: (1) _conversation_baseline reads get_conversation at query_database.py:221; (2) Agent.send_message loads it at agent.py:431 (the only other get_conversation in send_message besides the starter-UI branch at 301, which is not taken); (3) _trim_unanswered_tool_use reads it at query_database.py:285. So reads>=3 is the trim's read. Appended object() has no .role: _first_unanswered_tool_use does following.role at query_database.py:258 (inner loop from the unanswered assistant, since object() follows it) -> AttributeError, caught at 299-307 and logged 'could not be scanned' with the store class name, matching the test's breadcrumb. Unarmed reads (_seed, _history, armed=False after the call) return super().get_conversation, the real conversation. The rejection line (truncate_messages -> bool) concerns a different subject and does not apply.

claim: The Anthropic request builder replays an assistant message from `provider_content` when it has one, so its `tool_use` blocks reach the API even when `tool_calls` is empty.
source_excerpt:
Both sources count: the Anthropic request builder replays an assistant
    message from ``provider_content`` when it has one, so its ``tool_use``
    blocks reach the API even when ``tool_calls`` is empty.
verify_hint: Check `_build_payload` in `src/sqllens/agent/integrations/anthropic/llm.py` for how assistant messages with `provider_content` are serialized.
evidence: llm.py:158-167 _build_payload: for role=='assistant' with provider_content not None, it deep-copies provider_content and appends it as the assistant message content, never consulting tool_calls. Only thinking/redacted_thinking blocks are filtered (older turns), so tool_use blocks are kept; the branch continues before the tool_calls serialization path. Claim holds even with empty tool_calls. The rejection line concerns truncate_messages, unrelated.

claim: The answered check matches the Anthropic API rule: every tool_use id must be answered by tool messages in the run directly after the assistant message, which the builder merges into the next user message's tool_result blocks.
verify_against: `_build_payload` in anthropic/llm.py (how consecutive role=tool messages become tool_result blocks)
verify_hint: Check `_build_payload` in `src/sqllens/agent/integrations/anthropic/llm.py` for grouping of tool messages after an assistant message.
evidence: query_database.py:243-263 (_first_unanswered_tool_use) collects ids from the assistant message, then walks messages[index+1:] collecting tool_call_id from consecutive role=='tool' messages, breaking at the first non-tool message; unanswered if ids not subset of answered. anthropic/llm.py:169-190 (_build_payload) groups consecutive role=='tool' messages directly into a single user message of tool_result blocks keyed by tool_call_id. This matches the claim: a tool_use is answered only by tool messages in the run directly after the assistant message. Absolute-claim trace: an assistant tool_use followed by an intervening user/assistant message then a tool message. The checker breaks at the intervening message, so it is unanswered, matching the API rule. Minor edge: the builder drops tool messages with falsy tool_call_id (llm.py:174), while the checker treats a None id as answerable by a None tool message (query_database.py:238-239,260). This needs a tool_use block with no id, which the API would reject anyway, and no shipped producer is shown creating one, so it does not break the claim. The rejection line about truncate_messages return values is unrelated to this claim.

claim: `truncate_messages(conversation_id, user_id, length)` is synchronous, returns bool True when it dropped messages, and raises `ConversationOwnerMismatchError` on owner mismatch.
verify_hint: Check `truncate_messages` in `src/sqllens/conversation_store.py` lines ~98-130.
evidence: conversation_store.py:98-143: truncate_messages is a plain `def` (synchronous), signature (conversation_id, user_id, length) -> bool; returns True after `del conversation.messages[length:]` (line 139-143), False for unknown id or length >= len; raises ConversationOwnerMismatchError when conversation.user.id != user_id (135-136). Also raises ValueError on negative length, which is an extra not contradicting the claim. Rejection line (declares -> bool at 98-122) confirmed by head bytes.

claim: When send_message raises, the trim runs and the original exception re-raises into the existing handlers, so the caller sees the same RuntimeError with `_INTERNAL_ERROR_MESSAGE` as before; an error answer still yields `AgentRunError` with `SQL execution error: ` prefix.
verify_hint: Check the `except UnsafeSqlError` / `except Exception` handlers and the error-answer path after the try in `query_database_impl_with_widgets`.
evidence: query_database.py:618-628: inner try/except Exception around send_message awaits _trim_unanswered_tool_use (when baseline_user and queued_id set) then bare `raise`, re-raising the original exception into the outer handlers. Those are unchanged: UnsafeSqlError/RlsError -> RuntimeError(str(e)) (645-656), and generic Exception -> RuntimeError(_INTERNAL_ERROR_MESSAGE) (657-662). _trim_unanswered_tool_use (266-336+) is documented and implemented to never raise Exception: get_conversation, message scan, truncate lookup and truncate call are each guarded and logged, so the trim cannot replace the original error (only the `agent.conversation_store` attribute read at 283 is unguarded, but the baseline read already uses that store). Error-answer path: after the successful loop, trim runs (629-631), then components_to_blocks and `if is_error: raise AgentRunError(f"{_SQL_EXECUTION_ERROR_PREFIX}{answer}", ...)` (702-708) is unchanged. The rejection line about truncate_messages -> bool is consistent with the head bytes and does not affect this claim.

claim: The `_Messages.create` stub accepts the kwargs the real `AnthropicLlmService` passes to `client.messages.create` with `stream_responses=False`, and `AnthropicMessage.model_validate` output matches what the service parses.
verify_hint: Check `AnthropicLlmService` in `src/sqllens/agent/integrations/anthropic/llm.py` for `self._client.messages.create` usage and response parsing.
evidence: llm.py:78 send_request calls self._client.messages.create(**payload); payload (llm.py:237-256) has model, messages (list of role/content dicts), max_tokens, optional temperature/extra_body/tools/tool_choice/system. Stub create(**kwargs) accepts all of these and reads kwargs['messages'][-1]['role'/'content'], with _text_of handling str or block-list content. Test sets stream_responses=False (test:155) so the non-streaming path is used. Stub returns AnthropicMessage.model_validate with id, role, model, content (text/tool_use blocks), stop_reason, stop_sequence, type, usage; llm.py _parse_message_content (269-314) reads typed block .type/.text/.name/.id/.input via getattr, resp.usage.input_tokens/output_tokens (85-90), stop_reason (97), and _provider_content uses block.model_dump (261-267), all satisfied by the validated Message. The rejection line concerns truncate_messages and does not cover this claim.

claim: Replacing `agent.tool_registry.execute` with a raising function makes the real Agent return an error answer (leading to AgentRunError with 'SQL execution error: ') after saving the assistant tool_use and without saving a tool message.
verify_hint: Check how `send_message` in `src/sqllens/agent/core/agent/agent.py` calls `tool_registry.execute` and handles its exception.
evidence: agent.py:701 adds the assistant tool_use message before the tool loop; agent.py:861 awaits self.tool_registry.execute(tool_call, context) with no local try/except, so a raising replacement propagates before conversation.add_message(tool_response_message) at :1048 (no tool message saved). Agent.send_message (agent.py:174-227) catches Exception and yields an 'Error Processing Message' status card with status 'error'. _format.py:596,715 recognises that card title with status 'error' as the agent error, and query_database.py:702-708 then raises AgentRunError(_SQL_EXECUTION_ERROR_PREFIX + answer), where the prefix is 'SQL execution error: ' (query_database.py:93). The test (test_query_database_tool_history.py:236-253) matches this path. The later trim of the unanswered tool_use is the separate behaviour the test goes on to assert.

claim: `_RaisingReadStore` assumes the trim's get_conversation is the third read of the call (baseline, agent load, trim).
source_excerpt:
# The baseline read and the agent's own load come first; the
            # third read of the call is the trim's.
verify_hint: Count `conversation_store.get_conversation` calls in `send_message` in `src/sqllens/agent/core/agent/agent.py` on the error path.
evidence: On the error path, query_database.py:607 calls _conversation_baseline, which does one store.get_conversation (line 221). Then agent.send_message makes exactly one get_conversation on the non-starter path (agent.py:431; the only other call, agent.py:301, is starter-UI only). The except at query_database.py:623-627 then calls _trim_unanswered_tool_use, whose get_conversation (line 285) is the third read. BoundedConversationStore.get_conversation is only defined (conversation_store.py:68) and nothing internal calls it, so the override counts no extra reads. The test arms the store after seeding (test file line 357), so reads counts from the call start, and `reads >= 3` raises at the trim's read, matching the comment at test lines 331-332.

claim: truncate_messages docstring: it has two production callers in tools/query_database.py, the cancellation handler and the trim.
source_excerpt:
It has two
        production callers in ``tools/query_database.py``: the cancellation
        handler, and the trim that removes an unanswered ``tool_use`` from a
        call that ended without cancellation.
verify_hint: Grep `truncate_messages` across `src/sqllens/` and check `_rollback_conversation` and `_trim_unanswered_tool_use`.
evidence: Grep of truncate_messages across head src/ shows the only call sites are in src/sqllens/tools/query_database.py: line 321 inside _trim_unanswered_tool_use (defined line 266, called at lines 625 and 630) and line 395 inside _rollback_conversation (defined line 359, called at line 641 in the run path). The other hits are comments, log strings, or the definition at conversation_store.py:98. So there are exactly two production callers in tools/query_database.py, the rollback (cancellation handler) and the trim of an unanswered tool_use, as the docstring says. I did not read the context around line 641 to confirm it sits in the cancellation handler; _rollback_conversation's own docstring says it is called from a cancelled task. The rejection line about a None return concerns a different property and does not affect this claim.
